svg.text: Everyday English - Idioms & slang
damn with faint praise
MEANING
To weaken someone or something with praise so
restrained that it implies a negative judgment.
IN CONTEXT
Calling her excellent presentation adequate damned it
with faint praise.
USAGE NOTE
The phrase describes an inferred attitude, not a literal
insult. Adequate can be neutral when basic sufficiency
is the real criterion; it becomes faint praise when
excellence is expected or deserved. Consider context,
tone, and comparison before inferring hostility. This
expression is more common in commentary than in
friendly small talk.
CONVERSATION
A: The review said the performance was competent.
B: That sounds positive at first.
A: But the reviewer called every other performer
outstanding.
B: In that context, competent rather damns her with
faint praise.
YOUR TURN
Explain the implication of The meal was edible in an
enthusiastic restaurant review. Model: It suggests mere
acceptability rather than enjoyment; the low standard
makes the apparent praise sound critical.
